verses.commentary: A prayer (tephillah) of Habakkuk. On shigionoth (perhaps a musical term indicating passionate, wandering style). The questioning prophet becomes the praying prophet. Dialogue with God matures into worship.

Lord, I have heard of your fame. I stand in awe of your deeds. Repeat them in our day. In wrath, remember mercy. The prophet heard God's answer and now responds. The request: ancient deeds renewed, judgment tempered with compassion.

God came from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran. Glory covered the heavens, praise filled the earth. Theophany begins. God approaches from the south, from Sinai's direction. The Exodus God returns.

Splendor like sunrise. Rays flash from his hand where power is hidden. The most powerful thing about God is concealed. What we see, the brilliant light, is just the covering. Hidden power exceeds visible glory.
Plague went before him, pestilence followed. Attendants of the divine warrior. The plagues of Egypt accompany the God of the Exodus. His arrival brings both destruction and deliverance.

He stood and shook the earth. He looked and made nations tremble. Ancient mountains crumbled, age old hills collapsed. But he marches on forever. Creation convulses; God is unperturbed. What seems permanent to us (mountains) is temporary to God.
Tents of Cushan in distress, dwellings of Midian in anguish. Nations around Sinai saw what Israel saw. Divine appearance affects all witnesses. No one observes unmoved.

Was your anger against rivers, Lord? Wrath against the sea? You rode horses and chariots to victory. The divine warrior on his war chariot. Rivers and sea recall the Reed Sea crossing. Cosmic battle imagery. Creation itself is the battlefield.
You uncovered your bow, called for many arrows. Split earth with rivers. Weaponry of the divine warrior. Even the terrain serves his purpose. Rivers become weapons. Geography submits to theology.
Mountains saw and writhed. Torrents swept by. The deep roared, lifted waves. Mountains personified in pain. Waters respond vocally. All creation participates in divine appearance.
Sun and moon stood still. Joshua 10 echoed. At the glint of flying arrows, lightning of flashing spear. Celestial bodies halt to witness divine warfare. Even time pauses for God.
In wrath you strode through earth, in anger you threshed nations. Threshing imagery: nations as grain under divine judgment. God walks through history separating wheat from chaff.

You came out to deliver your people, save your anointed. Crushed the leader of wickedness, stripped him head to foot. Judgment serves salvation. God fights against evil to rescue his own. The wicked ruler destroyed completely.

With his own spear you pierced his head. Warriors storming out to scatter, gloating over the wretched. The oppressor's weapon turns against him. Those who rejoiced in crushing the helpless are themselves crushed.
You trampled the sea with your horses, churning great waters. Sea symbolizes chaos, threat, enemy. God's horses tread on chaotic waters. What seems overwhelming to us is a path for God.

I heard and my heart pounded. Lips quivered, decay crept into bones, legs trembled. Yet I will wait patiently for calamity to come on the invading nation. Physical terror at theophany vision. But faith emerges from fear. Waiting replaces trembling.

Though fig tree does not bud, no grapes on vines, olive crop fails, fields produce no food, no sheep in pen, no cattle in stalls. Total agricultural collapse enumerated. Everything fails. Every source of sustenance removed.

Yet I will rejoice in the Lord, be joyful in God my Savior. The book's climax. Joy despite loss. Faith despite disaster. Worship despite circumstances. The righteous lives by faith (2:4) demonstrated in practice.

The Sovereign Lord is my strength. He makes my feet like deer's feet, enables me to tread on heights. For the director of music, on stringed instruments. Surefooted confidence. High places traversed safely. The questioning prophet ends as a singer of praise. Complaint becomes hymn. Wrestling becomes worship.
